5.1.3. Manipulations
5.1.3.1. Task A regulatory focus. The regulatory focus of Task A was
manipulated by modifying Task A framing in a manner consistent
with prior research (Freitas et al., 2002; Shah, Higgins, & Friedman,
1998). For those assigned to the promotion frame, Task A was
described as an opportunity to achieve success by successfully
completing the task. The task goal was presented in terms of
solutions found. For example, participants read: ‘‘Goal you want
to reach: Your goal is to answer all 17 clues using only 5 unique
words. You will successfully complete the task if you ﬁnd these 5
unique words.” This framing was reinforced when participants
were interrupted, with the experimenter telling them: ‘‘At this
point, I need to interrupt you on this task [. . .]. But I will give
you 5 more minutes at the end of the experiment for you to try
to ﬁnish this task and meet the target of answering all 17 clues with
only 5 unique words.”
To those assigned to the prevention frame, Task A was
described as a risk to fail by not completing the task. The task goal
was presented in terms of solutions left unfound. For example, par-
ticipants read: ‘‘Goal you need to reach: Your goal is to answer all
17 clues using only 5 unique words. You will fail to complete the
task if you don’t ﬁnd these 5 unique words.” This framing was also

DISCUSSION
Our findings show that the decrease seen in total
government school enrollments can be almost en-
tirely accounted for by a decrease in students en-
rolled in the mainstream. Whereas mainstream
enrollments as a percentage of total enrollments
decreased between 1997 and 2009, SC Secondary
and SSP enrollments increased. SC Elementary
enrollments fluctuated across the time period of
interest, thus resulting in an overall flat trend.

Confirmatory factor analysis
We tested our measurement model using CFA in MPlus version 7
(Muthén & Muthén, 1998–2012). For the indicators of the organiza-
tional identity latent variable, we formed three parcels on the basis
of the subscales of this measure, which is a recommended step given
that these item sets should share secondary covariance that would
otherwise distort the results of the CFA (Hall, Snell, & Foust, 1999).
Following best practices for parceling (Williams & O’Boyle, 2008), we
evaluated the reliability of each parcel. Specifically, the three parcels
consisted of the means of the three solidarity items (α = .91), the three
identity centrality items (α = .88), and the four identity satisfaction
items (α = .92). Because the constructive deviance and normative
conflict measures are not multidimensional, we used the individual
items as the indicators for their respective latent variables.

the data given the small sample size, χ2
